No game has ever been publicly decompiled within a month of release, and the best AI-agent precedent was about 2.5x too slow on a smaller, unencrypted PC target. Beyond that, a playable intro needs translation of the console graphics and OS APIs, plus a team willing to publish despite Take-Two's fast takedowns and lawsuits. The remaining probability comes mostly from lenient or erroneous resolution (a hybrid build, a static recompilation, or a hoax) and a small chance of a surprise private exploit plus a massive agent swarm.

The bar is only one person attending for one full day because of the market, and the creator is probably an organizer who can trace discount-code use and knows the small Bay Area/Manifold community. BTC sits near $74k with ~3 weeks left and needs a further ~12-13% fall to $65k on Binance BTC/USDT, a roughly 1.3-1.4σ move at current implied vol. Implied vol typically overstates realised vol, but November is clearly a higher-volatility, risk-off regime with large liquidation cascades, ETF outflows and Binance-specific stress, and any Binance-only wick counts. Supports at ~$73k and $70-72k, plus heavy put OI around $74k, mean a modest selloff likely stalls before $65k, and the status quo of ranging between $70k and $80k resolves NO. Starting from a ~37% challenger win rate in heavyweight title fights, I adjust down because Hokit has only about a year in the UFC, has never fought championship rounds, and is defensively porous: he absorbed ~175 significant strikes from Blaydes, and Gane has an 8-inch reach edge and elite kickboxing. YES requires a jump of +1.5 to +2.4 points from October's 55.5. That is a roughly one-standard-deviation-plus move and would push the index to its highest level since early 2022. October's gain was driven by production, inventories and supplier deliveries rather than new orders, while sentiment worsened and S&P Global's new-orders growth slowed. Falling oil and progress toward a US-Iran deal point to easing supplier delays and less precautionary inventory building, which would weigh on the headline. Upside paths exist (AI and defence capex, restocking from low customer inventories, renewed Hormuz disruption), but they are offset by mean reversion within the 54.5-55.6 range seen since July. No November regional data is out yet, so I stay close to the base rate with a slight downward tilt.

Ma has repeatedly chosen influence without a title. He denied returning in 2025 and remained untitled while widely described as the de facto decision-maker. Alibaba is thriving under Eddie Wu and Joe Tsai, so there is no crisis to justify a founder returning, and political sensitivity argues against a formal role. With about 31 days to close and no reports of any change as of Nov 10, the status quo is heavily favoured. The main residual risks are a surprise announcement with the mid/late-November results and a loose reading of 'clearly in charge' by the creator if new major-outlet reporting describes Ma as running Alibaba. Neither is likely, but together they put the probability modestly above the formal-appointment floor.

The Sep hike and Oct pause are locked in, so YES requires only a December hike. The committee is leaning hawkish: 16 of 18 participants projected another 2026 hike, two voters (including Cook) dissented for a hike in October, several regional presidents are publicly pushing for more, October payrolls were strong, and core PCE is rising. Major forecasters (JPMorgan, Commerzbank, MBA, Oxford) now expect December. The main risks are Warsh's non-committal, wait-and-see style; four weeks of data that could soften, especially with energy prices easing; and a Sep-2023-style failure to deliver the dotted hike. I weight these at roughly a quarter, slightly below the historical base rate.

Through Nov 9, the visible ChatGPT incidents (Nov 4, 5, 8, 9) all appear to be Minor/Degraded (yellow), so most likely 0 red days are on the board, though the status page couldn't be verified directly. With about 20 days left and a base rate near 3 red days/month, the expected remaining red days are about 1.8–2. Allowing for clustering, that gives roughly a 65% chance of ≤2 if none have occurred yet. If an unverified red day already exists (~23%), YES drops to about 40%. Sub-component outages turning the ChatGPT box red and time-zone edge cases add modest NO risk, while the mild first third of the month and the Thanksgiving week slightly favour YES.

Verstappen has finished on the podium in seven straight races, including two wins, and has a strong Vegas record (wins in 2023 and 2025, P5 in 2024), so his finishing pace comfortably clears a top-5 bar. The main risk is not finishing: the first-year Ford power unit has failed twice, the Brazil handling problem is unexplained, and Vegas brings safety-car chaos and plank-wear disqualification risk. I put that at about 11%. He is already over his engine allocation, so any further component change means a grid penalty, and recovering in a dry race is harder than in wet Brazil. Conditional on finishing, I estimate about 81% for a top 5 against Mercedes, Ferrari and McLaren. That gives roughly 0.72–0.73, just under the base rate from his recent form because of the reliability and penalty tails.

The only realistic YES path is a Colts-to-Packers trade made official around today's 4 p.m. ET deadline, because Taylor's new extension through 2028 with ~$39M guaranteed rules out free agency or release before Dec 1. If a trade happens, the Giants are the only team with a known concrete offer, while Green Bay lacks a 2027 first-round pick and hasn't been reported making a formal bid. The Jacobs exempt-list situation gives the Packers genuine motive, which keeps their conditional share around 15-25%. Multiplying gives roughly 5-7%, shaded slightly down because no 'Packers closing in' reports surfaced on deadline day.

PSG are in dominant form (4/4 UCL wins, 20 goals, 11 straight wins) and face a Roma side that concedes freely in Europe and has goalkeeper injury problems, which points to a home win in a likely open game. Pressure is intense: a wave election blamed partly on the Iran war, a privileged impeachment vote this week with reported GOP defections, Tillis and other GOP senators calling for a change, CBS reporting that Trump is privately polling advisers, and a named potential successor (DeSantis). Only about 2-3 chapters (1199, 1200, possibly leaks of 1201) can come out before close, and the Nov 15 break plus Oda's frequent breaks may shrink that further. The tentpole reference class with positive first reactions puts finishing above 77 at roughly even odds, and the franchise history (recent entries 64-70%) pulls slightly lower. The newest iPhone already ships Siri AI, which can reach personal data from many apps, Safari history, voicemail, past conversations and the current screen, and has per-app exclusion toggles. Every private poll and average gives PP+Vox about 190-205 seats, well above the 176 majority, so a Feijóo investiture with Vox votes is the dominant scenario. Spain's 2023 polling overstated the right by about 10 bloc seats, but overturning the current cushion needs roughly twice that error, and left fragmentation (Sumar collapse, Podemos near zero) reduces seat efficiency. Vox brinkmanship is more likely to delay a Feijóo investiture than to produce a Sánchez one. Small tail paths (a Junts reversal, a deadlock leading to a repeat election) keep the probability above a few percent.

Inter are clearly the stronger side on form (≈2.5 PPG, 2nd) while Atalanta sit 12th with five losses and a demoralising 0-3 home loss to Parma, and Inter have won their last three confirmed visits to Bergamo and nine straight H2H meetings. Against that, Inter's forward line is depleted (Lautaro returning from a month out, Thuram with a fresh hamstring issue, Bonny out, Stanković hurt) and the game falls straight after an international break with a Champions League match three days later. A draw resolves NO and carries a ~25% structural probability. Netting these, I land slightly below the reference-class away-win rate, near what a bookmaker line would likely imply.

The only professional tracking ($260-300M, recently revised down) sits well below the $360.1M bar, and no December opening has come within about 30% of it. The market reduces to a single Bo5 final on Nov 14 between BLG and Gen.G, with negligible 'Other' risk. No title match in history appears to have featured an ECO A00 opening, and both Gukesh and Sindarov are mainstream 1.e4/1.d4 players whose camps signal continuity rather than novelty first moves. A one-off classical surprise from a trailing Gukesh adds about 1–2%. Even then, transpositions often give the game a non-A00 code, which cuts the YES chance. Small additions come from lenient labeling by the resolver and from ambiguity about which 'World Championship 2026' counts.

With 19 days left, the status quo heavily favours NO. Russia publicly rejected a freeze and short-term ceasefires on Nov 9, refused to extend the Oleshky truce, and the Abu Dhabi talks just resumed with no sign of progress on the Donbas. The most plausible YES path is a short US-brokered nationwide pause, perhaps tied to a prisoner swap. A comprehensive framework with a dated ceasefire inside three weeks is very unlikely given the unresolved territorial issue. I keep a few percent for Trump's push for a headline win, Russia's recent battlefield setbacks, and the unknown day-two outcome.

Assuming the standard Polymarket exact-score list (all scores up to 3-3), YES requires one team to reach 4+ goals, which happens in roughly 10% of 2. Bundesliga matches. Karlsruhe's matches this season have been unusually high-scoring (3.5 goals/game, 3 of 11 with a 4+ team, including 4-0 and 2-5 at home), which nudges the estimate up. Osnabrück's modest away attack and the likely cagey relegation-six-pointer character pull it back toward the base rate. No-result scenarios resolve to 0-0, so they only cut against YES. A small allowance for a possibly shorter outcome list adds a fraction of a point.

Haaland cut his long hair to a near-buzz on 23 Aug 2026 and has said repeatedly he will let it grow back. A late-October report already describes a side-parting. Natural regrowth alone gives about 4-5 cm on top by late December, which most resolvers would read as 'let his hair grow' rather than a clean crew cut. The main YES paths are a deliberate re-buzz or regular short trims for anonymity or superstition, or a lenient resolver counting a tidy short crop as a crew cut. The regrowth evidence is secondary and partly unconfirmed, and the resolution criteria are vague, so I don't go below about 10%.

Confirmed pipeline hits have occurred roughly every 20 days during the current Houthi/Iraqi-militia campaign, and the Houthis explicitly claimed pumping-station targeting on 10 Nov, so a new qualifying impact in the remaining ~19 days is roughly a coin flip after discounting for interceptions, debris exclusions, sparse Saudi confirmation and a possible truce. If it opened before 9 Nov, the Saudi Energy Ministry-confirmed Medina strike (fire plus satellite-visible damage at Pumping Station 8) likely already resolves YES. Weighting about 37% on early creation times about 82% qualification, plus about 50% forward risk otherwise, gives about 0.64. The main downside risks are a Saudi-Houthi deal and Saudi wording that frames incidents as interceptions with debris fires.

Two independent Burgos polls (GAD3 10 Nov, University of Burgos 5 Nov) project PP 2, PSOE 1, Vox 1, which is an outright PP win, and a uniform-swing model from 2023 gives PP an 8-11 point lead in Burgos. Even a 2-2 split resolves YES as long as PP outpolls PSOE, and Burgos leans about 5-6 points more PP than the nation. A NO outcome requires PSOE to lead nationally by roughly 5 points, a 7+ point miss or swing against polls that all show PP ahead by 2-8 points, with 18 days left. BTC sits near $73.6k after a hot CPI print and needs to touch $85k (+15.5%) on CoinGecko within about 19 days. Resolution hinges almost entirely on the Dec 9 FOMC decision. The September projections implied one more 2026 hike, two members dissented for a hike in October, October CPI and payrolls both came in hot, and post-CPI Fed speakers are debating 25 vs 50bp; a reported Reuters poll has all economists expecting a hike. Evidence comes from secondary sources, which argues against going above 90%.

Apple (~$5.1T) leads Microsoft (~$4.0-4.1T) and Nvidia (~$3.9T after hours) by roughly 25-33% with only ~13 trading sessions left before the Nov 30 close. Historically, #1 changes only happen when the top two are within ~10%. Nvidia is in an unusually high-volatility regime: it lost ~25% in a week, and both the board decision on Huang and the Nov 17 earnings report fall in the window. A Huang retention plus a blowout quarter plus an Apple pullback could in principle close the gap, so I set P(NO) somewhat above the base rate. A Huang ouster, a muted earnings reaction, or Apple simply holding would all keep Apple #1, and Microsoft has no catalyst.

Florida is 5-4 and must win all three remaining regular-season games; any loss resolves NO. The first game is at No. 11 Kentucky, where Florida is roughly a 4-point underdog, implying about a 35% win chance; Florida's offense has collapsed (15 points and 5 INTs in two games, unsettled QB, WR injury), which offsets Kentucky's own 34-6 loss at Tennessee. Vanderbilt at home (~72%) and at an FSU team under an interim coach (~55%) are both winnable but far from certain, with Vanderbilt and FSU each playing for bowl eligibility. The independent product is about 14%, and the positive correlation between games roughly balances a small extra discount for Florida's slump.

On every plausible reading of 'gross', 2026 beats 2022 after inflation by a wide margin: about $13-15bn cycle revenue against about $8.6-8.7bn in real 2022 terms, and about $5bn tickets/hospitality against about $1.07bn. Even the least favourable comparison (pre-tournament 2026 tournament-only estimate of $8.9bn against the full 2022 cycle inflated) still comes out YES, and actuals reportedly beat budget. Attendance roughly doubled at much higher prices, which supports the revenue reports independently. The residual risk is mainly resolver ambiguity (profit or economic-impact readings) and the 2026 figures being unaudited press reports, but the margins are large enough that sizeable errors would not flip the outcome.

Tirante's ranking edge is largely cancelled by the surface: he is about 40% career on hard and indoor courts and has never reached a hard-court semifinal, while Shevchenko has a strong indoor record (Basel QF over Fritz, Metz SF) and is in hot form after beating Ruud and dropping just one set all week. Against that, Shevchenko has played five matches in about five days, and the day after a big upset he often comes out flat, while Tirante is fresh after a walkover and won their only meeting 6-3, 6-3 on hard courts. The one readable expert pick favours Shevchenko. Walkover risk (resolving 50-50) is small, about 1-2%. Net, I put Tirante slightly below even.

Universal child care is Mamdani's signature delivered policy and his standard justification for taxing the wealthy, which is the natural DealBook topic with Sorkin. Sorkin himself raised child care as a business-retention issue in their January Squawk Box interview. A 25-40 minute session gives many openings, including his habitual 'child care, housing, transit' agenda list. The main risks are a no-show or cancellation (~7%), which resolves this market NO, and a conversation dominated by 2028, Trump, COPA or crypto in which he cites program names like 2-K/3-K instead of the phrase. Combining ~93% appearance with ~86% conditional mention gives about 80%.

Multiple credible sources (CNBC citing sources, plus roundups) put pricing on Wed Nov 18 and first trade on Thu Nov 19, so YES needs a one-day slip to Fri Nov 20. Such exact one-day slips are rare for mega-IPOs; strong demand (several times oversubscribed, $26B strategic anchors) and the SpaceX precedent favour sticking to the schedule. The WSJ's earlier 'Thursday or Friday' window and an ambiguous Hargreaves Lansdown reference to Nov 20 pricing keep Friday a live possibility. A possible range raise or AI-selloff volatility could add a day, but delays more often run to zero days or weeks. I estimate about 8%.

Indiana is 8-1 and must win all three remaining games: USC at home, Washington away, and Purdue at home. USC is the main hurdle: Indiana is a 7.5-point favorite, and FPI (78%) and SP+ (74%) put it at about 75%. Washington at 5-4 on the road is about 80%, and Purdue is about 95%. The product is roughly 0.57. Hoover's arm injury and an offense that needed overtime twice in a row add some correlated downside, but his absence from the initial injury report is mildly encouraging.

Spark has gone 71 days without an update after a monthly summer rhythm, and since 1.3 Meta has restructured around Muse Wonder with distilled models under new names (Ember, Spark Open, specialized product models), which suggests the Spark numbered line may be frozen or renamed. The promised 'smaller models soon' appear fulfilled by Ember (Nov 9) and the specialized models, removing the main near-term catalyst. Only about 18 days remain, the Thanksgiving week is likely dead, and previews or third-party listings don't count. The muse-spark-1.4-contributor ID and Spark 1.3's poor cost position versus Ember keep a real tail: a Wonder-distilled Spark 1.4 refresh is plausible. However, the ID has sat at zero usage for two months, which weakens it as a signal.

Hamilton usually qualifies in the top 6 in a front-running Ferrari, which caps his gain at about +5 and rarely wins this market. Most YES probability comes from a deep start (about 15–20% at chaotic, cold Vegas qualifying, or via a non-PU component penalty) followed by a charge, and he wins about 35–40% of the time from there. Russell's reported Vegas PU penalty would likely put a dominant Mercedes deep on the grid as a strong competitor, and Verstappen showed +19 in Brazil. The midfield-to-podium path from 2024 adds about 1–2%, and tie splits add a sliver. Total is about 7%.

Public polls since late October put Vox at ~17.5-20% and 58-72 seats, with a central estimate around 63-67; no poll's central estimate falls in 56-60. I shade the centre slightly down to ~64 because 40dB (61 seats, falling trend) and the CIS (17.1%) point lower and Spain has a history of late tactical consolidation toward the PP, as in 2023. That is partly offset by the post-Urda anti-government mood and Vox matching or beating its polls in the 2026 regional elections. Applying a historical seat-error spread of about 6-7 seats to a centre near 64 gives roughly 17-20% for the 5-seat bracket below the centre. The brief's figures come from search summaries only, so individual numbers carry moderate uncertainty, but the overall picture is consistent across pollsters.

The structural prior strongly favors a woman, and Trump's female press secretaries have mostly been blonde, which alone would suggest ~50%. However, the freshest and most specific reporting (Fox News, Nov 10, echoed by Political Wire and Washington Times) says sources expect Trump to pick a man, with all named frontrunners male (Ferguson, Jennings, Cheung, Boyle, Fleischer). I put P(woman) around 35-40%, discounting the anonymous sourcing given Trump's erratic process. Conditional on a woman, blonde candidates (Kelly, Miller, Harp) outnumber non-blonde ones, but Alvarez (dark-haired) has been called a favorite, so ~60%. The main YES path is Anna Kelly being elevated or named acting; no acting designation has occurred in 4 weeks.

On Oct 30 swaps priced about a 57% chance of a December hike. Since then the October jobs report missed badly (-4.7k jobs, unemployment 6.7%, a third straight monthly decline), GDP has stalled, and Brent has fallen about 20% to the low-to-mid $90s, so market odds have likely swung toward a hold. Against that, BoC communications on Nov 3 and Nov 10 still say further hikes may be needed, the MPR projects about 3.5% CPI, and historically the BoC has always followed a first hike with a second. The oil path is a genuine two-way risk, with an 80% chance of renewed fighting cited by Rapidan. The Nov 16 CPI, Nov 30 GDP and Dec 4 jobs releases are all still ahead. Overall I lean modestly toward a hold, with substantial uncertainty.

First-wave polls are unusually strong at 62-69% yes, with 74% firm intentions per gfs.bern and majorities in every party camp, which fits the profile of initiatives that held up. Applying the typical ~10-point campaign decline gives a vote-day yes of about 55-59%. At that level a cantonal majority is likely but not guaranteed, given rural German-speaking and possibly Latin cantons. The No side is underfunded, but the Federal Council, Parliament, SVP, FDP and Mitte all oppose, and animal and agrarian initiatives have historically faded. No second-wave polling is available yet, so meaningful uncertainty remains.

Reaching $400M requires beating the 4-month-old record by 11% with record previews (~$75-80M+), and doing so without IMAX screens, on a pre-Christmas weekend with schools in session, with a 165-minute runtime and Dune 3 competing for adults and premium screens. Presales are genuinely record-pace (~$65M domestic ~50 days out, premium shows selling out), and fan-driven event films typically beat tracking by 15-30%. But mainstream projections of $250-300M only reach about $330-390M even after a typical beat. The most bullish $400M+ claims come from enthusiast trackers and aggregators rather than verified trade tracking. My central estimate is about $340M with a wide spread, which gives roughly 15-20% for $400M or more.

Lai Jui-lung leads in nearly every public poll, including a +7 lead in the KMT-leaning UDN poll, and voters expect him to win by about 49% to 21%. Kaohsiung's post-2010 electorate is structurally DPP, Ko lost by about 18 points in the strong KMT year of 2022, and the 2026 national environment is improving for the DPP. Ko's paths are a 2018-style polling miss combined with weak green consolidation after a divisive primary, stronger KMT–TPP vote pooling, or a late scandal. These are real but limited with about two weeks left and no neutral post-debate poll showing a tie. An open seat and the narrower-than-usual margins justify going a little above the 12% historical base rate.

Silver sits essentially at the $50 strike with 17 days left, and one-sigma moves are about ±$4.50, so the outcome is close to a coin flip. The latest Asian-session quotes (~$50.5) are slightly above the strike, but the Nov 12 NY close was just under $50. The macro backdrop leans bearish: hawkish Fed talk of 50bp or two more hikes, a 19-month dollar high, rising real yields, and a strong 2026 downtrend with weak positive momentum effects. Offsetting this, a December hike is already fully priced, positioning is light, $48-50 is well-watched support, and post-crash rebounds can be sharp. I shade slightly below 50% for trend and macro, with residual uncertainty about the resolution feed (likely Pyth spot) and current spot.

PSG are clearly the stronger side, on an 11-match winning run and deep enough to win comfortably even without several stars, and they have won 5 of their last 6 league visits to Nice. Against that, Nice are in excellent form (5 wins in 6, top 6, unbeaten at home) and will treat this as their biggest home game. The match falls right after an international break that took about 10 PSG players away and four days before a Champions League home game against Roma, which raises the risk of rotation and flat performances. A draw resolves NO, and Ligue 1 draws run at about 25%, which caps PSG's win probability even when they are favourites. Nice's defensive absences (Bombito, Mendy, Abdi) partly offset their form, so I settle slightly below the usual market level for PSG away to a top-half side.

The US federal government is absent and hostile, and India's environment minister explicitly said India will not sign any pledge, so YES runs almost entirely through China. China already targets 35% electrification by 2030 and called the goal its 'policy direction', and Türkiye is a friendly host, which lifts China above its usual near-zero rate for these pledges. But China's consistent pattern (e.g., backing COP28 tripling in substance but not signing) and its reported 'stopped short of endorsing' stance as of 5 Nov point to NO. With one week left, a possibly delayed backer list, and a resolution bar requiring formal confirmation, I put the total around 11%, including a small allowance for India reversing and for a lenient resolver counting US subnational signers.

The generic away-win rate in UCL league-phase games is about 29%, and the specific factors roughly cancel out. United's squad quality, their high scoring, their need for league-phase points, and Sporting's own coaching change (Fonseca) plus a possible rotation before the Porto Clássico all favour United. Against that, United's dire league form (18th), leaky defence, injuries (Baleba out, Maguire and Shaw doubtful), fatigue three days after Anfield, and Pochettino having almost no training time all favour Sporting, who are a strong European home side. A draw makes up a large share of the NO outcome. The pre-mortem suggests a United win via a new-manager bounce in an open game is a normal one-in-three outcome rather than a shock, so I stay near the base rate.

The September dots implied exactly one more 25 bp hike, two voters dissented for a hike in October, and October CPI and jobs data came in hot, so a December hike is the strong base case. The main risk to this exact-25 bracket is a 50 bp move: Waller's stated trigger for considering 50 (core CPI of 0.3% or more) was met, Logan cited 'at least 50 bp', and BofA flags rising risk. However, a 50 bp step right after a hold, with no forward guidance from Warsh and Hammack reportedly preferring smaller steps, has little precedent. A hold is a smaller risk, given Warsh's October hold despite the dots, Trump's pressure, and possible weak data or shocks. Evidence comes from search summaries only, which warrants some extra humility.

The album needs #1 on both the Nov. 21 and Nov. 28 charts. HITS projects Lil Baby's FRESH ahead 64k to 57.2k for Nov. 21, and leads of that size rarely flip. Possible bulk sales would make a flip even less likely. If Rodrigo does upset FRESH, the Nov. 13 release slate is weak, so holding Nov. 28 is likely (~70-75%), though her units keep declining. Multiplying ~13% by ~72% gives roughly 9%.

Illinois needs just one win in three games: at No. 4 UCLA (about +10, ~21%), home vs 7-2 Iowa (~41%), and at a fading Northwestern (~48%). If the games were independent, the chance of losing all three would be about 24%. Correlation from injuries and true team strength raises that to roughly 26%. Injuries to both top running backs plus a questionable center and defensive lineman are meaningful negatives, but the lines and models largely price them in. The four-game winning streak and a stable program argue against a collapse, so I land at about 74%.

The best-confirmed close is $166.19 on Nov 12, about 3.7% above the strike, but conflicting Nov 13 snapshots ($159-168) mean the true starting point may be only slightly above $160. With an earnings release on Nov 17 (the first without Huang), ongoing scandal and regulatory headlines, and realized vol of 60-80%, the distribution of outcomes is very wide, so a small cushion translates into only a modest edge. Strong dip-buying, a cheap forward multiple and a $108B guide that is likely to be beaten support a rebound. Heavy negative momentum, a wave of downgrades and NVDA's tendency to fall after recent reports offset that. Net, YES is slightly favored, but it is close to a coin flip.

Husted's term reportedly ends Dec 15, and Brown expects to be sworn in by Dec 15-16. The ~4.8-point margin rules out recounts, and Ohio certification should finish in early December. The binding risk is the Senate not sitting Dec 15-18. The earlier calendar ran through Dec 18, and an outgoing GOP majority racing to confirm ~25 judges has strong reason to stay, but a funding/NDAA deal around Dec 11 could still send members home early, as in 2016. Delaying Brown gains Republicans little because the seat goes vacant anyway, and the 2020 Kelly precedent shows opposite-party majorities seat winners promptly. Residual risks are the unverified Dec 15 date in a narrow four-day window and the earlier UTC close time.

Expert ratings and the 16-seat KMT starting position put the DPP about 3 seats short of parity. Closing that gap requires sweeping the toss-ups, holding every Lean DPP seat, and flipping at least two Lean KMT races. DPP-leaning trends are real: the KMT's poor favorability, KMT-TPP splits in Hsinchu County and Yilan, a New Taipei lead, and tightening in Keelung and Taitung. Correlated poll error could flip several races together, and ties likely go to the DPP alphabetically. However, many favorable polls are DPP-commissioned, the ruling party usually suffers a midterm penalty, and the KMT leads in Taichung, Taoyuan and Taipei. A DPP plurality or tie is plausible but clearly less likely than not.

Historically, DFW sees a trace or more of snow in roughly one November in six, almost always in the second half of the month, so the unconditional chance for this window is about 13%. The near-term forecast removes most of the window. The coming cool spell keeps metro lows in the 40s-50s with no moisture, and the CPC 6-10 and 8-14 day outlooks favor above-normal temperatures through about Nov 26-27, with no sign of early-season cold outbreaks. The remaining live window is roughly Nov 28-30, which is beyond forecast skill and is worth about 2-3% at climatological rates. A small extra amount covers a bust in the warm outlook and the lenient trace rule, under which flurries mixed with rain count. The strong El Niño adds subtropical moisture but mainly affects December-February.

The array averages six brand YoY indices equally, so the shrinking brands (Celsius brand ~92, Rockstar ~85, C4 likely sub-100) offset much of Monster's (~112) and Red Bull's (~104) growth, and the outcome hinges on Alani Nu. Alani grew ~+58% all-channel in Q3 2026, and its c-store growth is plausibly higher because the PepsiCo store-delivery rollout was still ramping in late 2025, giving a low November 2025 base. Plugging in the latest trends gives a central array estimate of about 107-108, but Alani at ~140 would put it below 105. Unknowns about Carbon Arc's data (panel vs scanner, brand mapping), the absence of any historical array values, and the chance that Kalshi set the strike near the current level all widen the distribution. Strong category momentum through October 2026 tilts modestly toward YES.

A December hike is strongly signalled: September dots imply one more 25bp move, both October dissents favoured 25bp, and the Reuters poll is unanimous for 4.00-4.25%. The main threat to YES is size: Waller explicitly said a 50bp hike should be considered after core CPI ran ~0.3% again, and Logan wants faster moves, so a 50bp outcome is a genuine ~19% tail, especially if October PCE or November payrolls run hot. Warsh appears less hawkish than the committee (AI-disinflation view, political pressure against hikes), Hammack prefers small steps and Goolsbee won't back 50, which anchors 25bp as the consensus compromise. A hold (~10%) remains possible given Warsh's October skip, an equity/AI selloff, or falling oil, but would be a large credibility reversal. Evidence is second-hand and excludes futures pricing, so I avoid going higher.

Asahifuji is 5-1 with nine bouts left, one behind a 6-0 Wakatakakage, alongside Enho and probably Tobizaru, in an unusually strong juryo field that includes six wrestlers dropped from makuuchi. His elite prospect record (four straight division titles, record-tying rise) and soft low-rank schedule justify sitting above the average-chaser base rate. However, week 2 will pit him against former makuuchi wrestlers where his edge is much smaller, a playoff loss resolves NO, and he showed a knee concern after Day 6. Wakatakakage's fragile legs give a meaningful path for the leader to fade, which keeps Asahifuji in the high teens rather than lower.

YES requires Act III to come out by Fri Dec 11 and then debut at No. 1. As of Nov 14 there is no date, the album has already slipped once, and only four Friday release dates remain, though she has surprise-dropped albums before. Even with a release, her first-week numbers are falling (64k for MEGAN), her freestyle singles have peaked around No. 64, and mid-December charts are crowded with holiday catalog titles and holdovers. Multiplying a ~22% release chance by a ~13% chance of reaching No. 1 gives about 3%. Leftover uncertainty about an unreported announcement keeps the estimate from going lower.

Only ~16 days remain, including Thanksgiving week, and the status quo of no senior round is strongly favoured. On Nov 12-13 Trump publicly said the US doesn't need a deal and sidelined Vance. Iran's Araghchi and Rezaei flatly denied plans for a Vance-Rezaei meeting, and Ghalibaf reiterated the 7 preconditions. Offsetting this, Qatar is actively mediating, Bloomberg and CNN describe quiet progress, the WSJ says Trump is privately open, and Trump's positions can flip abruptly. The lenient indirect-shuttle criterion (same city, same day, mediated) lowers the bar compared with a direct meeting. A YES needs a fast reversal by both sides plus a scheduled Doha-type round within two weeks, which I put at roughly 1 in 9.

The resolving reference class of recent family animated sequels puts roughly 40% above 80, but video-game adaptations and this franchise sit below that. AB2, the best film in the series, opened at 81-82% and then drifted down to 72%, which suggests the series' typical quality lands in the 70s. The strict threshold (80 = NO) and the usual downward drift by the Monday checkpoint both make YES harder. The new studio (DNEG), the Paramount handoff and the mixed trailer reception add downside risk. The carried-over writer and director and the strong recent run of family animation keep a meaningful YES path open. No reviews or embargo info exist yet, so I stay close to the adjusted base rate.

Israel resumed air and drone strikes in south Lebanon from 4 Nov 2026, with qualifying strikes on at least 6 of the 10 days to 13 Nov. The IDF's forward-defence posture and a permissive Israeli government favour this continuing. However, 28 Nov is 14 days away, and the June-October period shows Israel can sustain weeks with almost no airstrikes, possibly again under US pressure around Waltz's visit or during coalition formation. Even under the current regime, many days involve only artillery, demolitions or gunfire, which do not qualify. Escalation (IDF casualties, an expanded operation, the Iran front) is a meaningful tail that would make a strike near-certain. Small resolution risks (strikes only inside the occupied zone, grenade-dropping quadcopters) trim the estimate slightly.

A misspelling of 'Neuman' as 'Newman' or 'Neumann' probably exists somewhere across his 2022, 2024 and 2026 coverage, given how common the competing spelling is. But the market resolves on someone finding and showing an example, and search engines treat the spellings as the same, so errors are hard to find. The market appears still unresolved after about six months, which suggests no accepted example has turned up yet, and this is real evidence toward NO. With 16 days left and Neuman out of the race, new coverage and new errors are unlikely. A possibly motivated or generous creator (the companion Newman-confusion market and the democrats4neuman site hint at a candidate-adjacent creator) keeps YES plausible.

The main YES path is a major Israeli or joint US–Israeli strike on Iran's interior before Nov 30. Historically that almost always triggers a full Tehran FIR closure within hours, and a closure of even a few hours qualifies. Israel is visibly preparing (cabinet meeting Nov 15), talks are stalled and Iran just hit at a US site in Bahrain. Against that, Netanyahu is a caretaker PM facing internal military and political resistance, Trump is signalling restraint while Qatar mediates, and only ~16 days remain. I put a large strike wave at ~25% and closure given a strike at ~80%, plus a few percent for a precautionary or salvo-related closure. The recent pattern of limited US strikes in the south has produced no general closure and anchors the status-quo NO.

Miller Lite's underlying 2026 dollar trend is roughly -5% to -10%, which implies an index of about 90-95, and Carbon Arc's own recent readings appear to be in the high 80s to low 90s. Losing a Saturday versus November 2025, plus possible late-month data lag, takes off a couple of points, so I centre near 87-88. The receipt panel is noisy: August's strike ladder was centred near 83 and it resolved only above 79, so a print at or below 82 is a real tail. Molson Coors reported improving Miller Lite share trends in Q3, a mild support. Overall the line sits about one standard deviation below the expected value, giving around 80-85% for YES.

The flash for September 2026 is -0.1%, so YES requires the official print to be -0.3% or lower, roughly a 0.15pp+ downside miss versus the unrounded flash. Flash errors are usually within ±0.1pp, which makes this a minority outcome. Post-flash data lean mildly negative: wholesale volume fell 0.2% after the flash counted wholesale as an offset, manufacturing volume is likely slightly down, and hours worked plunged 1.5%. August's 0.2pp downside miss shows such errors happen in the current weakening phase. However, the flash already had the LFS hours data and the manufacturing weakness, and retail's +0.7% nominal advance should support services. On balance, YES is a bit above the pure base rate.

Watson (WTA 364, career-high 38) is the clear quality favourite and showed top-level form beating Samsonova two weeks ago, while Sawashiro (ranked ~680-800) has been routed by every clearly stronger opponent she faced in 2026. However, Sawashiro is an 18-year-old home junior on her best-ever run, having won three W50 rounds, so her ranking likely understates her current level. Watson's 2026 results are inconsistent, and her three-set quarterfinal adds some fatigue risk. Women's matches are volatile, and the brief could not confirm live status, scores or seedings, so I stay near the ranking-model base rate rather than going higher.

The 2026 evidence moderately favors parallel trends: METR's risk report shows a roughly 2.8x constant messy/clean level gap, the internal frontier reportedly shows no gap, and RLI messy-work scores reportedly grew fast. However, the HCAST suite is saturated and noisy, no messiness-split doubling-time analysis appears to have been published, and the author had already discounted similar 2025 in-suite messiness evidence because of small n and the low messiness ceiling. WTI settled at $88.56 on Nov 13. The January contract likely becomes the Active Month around Nov 17 at a backwardation discount, so a touch of $120 needs a gain of roughly 36-38% in about 11 sessions, including Thanksgiving-shortened days. Throughout the 2026 Iran war, even with Hormuz effectively closed in March-April, WTI peaked around $114.6-117.6 and never reached $120, and the October escalation topped out near $110. Current momentum and fundamentals point down: two straight weekly losses, the IEA now projecting a surplus, OPEC output near pre-war levels, US crude inventory builds, and Trump signalling no new strikes while Qatar mediates. The tail risk is real: ongoing tanker attacks, a possible resumption of US strikes, and Iranian retaliation against Gulf infrastructure could cause a large overnight gap. Even that would probably need to exceed the worst shocks of 2026 to print $120 so soon.
